newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Soquimich to invest $240 mln in '97.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Soquimich to invest $240 mln in '97.

text.p: Chile's largest fertilizer-maker Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile SA (Soquimich) will invest $240 million this year, said CEO Patricio Contesse.
"In 1996, we invested $180 million and this year we will invest $240 million," Contesse told reporters at the company's shareholders' meeting.

Soquimich, which produces nitrates, iodine and lithium, plans to invest $500 million in the 1997-1999 period. Around $200 million of this will be spent on the company's recently announced plans to move into the cement business, he said.
"We are able to compete in cement as we believe we will be by far the lowest cost producers," he said.
Most of the investment on cement, which will mainly supply Chile's booming construction sector, will be spent in 1998 and 1999.
Soquimich plans to finance the investment from its own resources and does not intend to issue bonds or a third series of American Depositary Receipts, said Contesse.
The remaining $300 million from its investment plan will be spent on the Minsal lithium and nitrates project, and other investments in nitrates, potash and iodine schemes.
"This year we will produce 350,000 tonnes of potassium chloride and we hope to increase this to 500,000 tonnes within two years," said Contesse.
Lithium output from Minsal, which is currently 9,000 tonnes a year, will rise to 18,000 tonnes a year from October, he said.
The company's most important project under construction at Minsal is a scheme to produce potassium sulphate at the mine, which lies on a dry salt lake in the northern Atacama Desert.
"We expect this to be in production at the end of this year or towards the beginning of the next," he said.
The production of potassium sulphate will churn out as a byproduct 16,000 tonnes a year of boric acid.
"All these products will complement our existing range of fertilizers and chemicals which go to industry," said Contesse. ((-- Paulina Modiano, Santiago newsroom, 562-699-5595 x212))
